thread:
sophie_cs: Heads-up — Rivertown is hitting intermittent preflight failures during onboarding. Browser SDK sees bursts of 429s and occasional 401s when they scale up headless tests. Can we triage?

rivertown_lead: Yep, reproducer: running 200 parallel preflights, ~30% fail with 429, a few 401s. Token refresh looks normal in app logs.

devin_sdk: :eyes: can you paste the exact preflight request and response headers? Also what SDK version?

rivertown_lead: SDK v0.18.3 (browser). Sample curl we use for repro:```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $EPHEMERAL" -H "Origin: https://app.rivertown.com" https://api.redwood-inference/v1/preflight```Response snippets:```HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests\nRetry-After: 1\nX-Request-Id: hq-9f3\n---\nHTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized\nWWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm=\"redwood\"\nX-Request-Id: hq-9f8```

sophie_cs: They hit this during our guided checklist step 3 (parallel warmup). Renewal at month end — need quick mitigations for onboarding to finish.

alex_eng: Thanks. Two immediate ideas: 1) reduce concurrent preflight window and add jitter when obtaining ephemeral tokens; 2) enable client-side preflight coalescing (single token fetch per origin per N ms). Can you show the token refresh code?

rivertown_lead: Token code is pretty standard, we call /session/create per tab then attach ephemeral token to preflight. We have no local cache across workers.

devin_sdk: Ok likely thundering herd on creating ephemeral tokens + upstream rate limits. Short-term: implement a tiny in-memory token lease with 2500ms TTL so concurrent requests reuse the same token. Also add linear jitter to refresh to avoid simultaneous refresh.

alex_eng: Also check the preflight route — we recently rolled a stricter rate limit for unauthenticated preflight bursts. If you can share X-Request-Id from failing requests I can trace in logs.

rivertown_lead: Pasted two ids above (hq-9f3, hq-9f8). We're running workaround now (serialize token fetch) and will report.

deploy-bot: NOTICE: new rate-limit config rolled to preflight-service at 2026-03-20T22:15Z (rule id preflight-burst-3s).

devin_sdk: That deploy-bot message is probably the culprit — rule reduces allowed preflight per origin over 3s window. Short-term options: 1) use server-side warmup instead of browser headless parallelism; 2) increase client-side splay/jitter; 3) request a temporary quota bump for the onboarding run.

sophie_cs: I'll ask RevOps for a temporary quota bump for Rivertown and relay the deploy-bot info. Can you also add suggested client snippet for token cache?

devin_sdk: Sure — tiny pseudo-snippet we sent often:```js// simple in-memory leaselet lease = null;async function getEphemeral(){ if(lease && Date.now() < lease.exp) return lease.token; lease = {token: await fetch('/session/create'), exp: Date.now()+2500}; return lease.token;}```This reduces parallel token fanout.

alex_eng: If they still see 401s after token caching, check clock skew on their CI runners — ephemeral token TTL is short and clock drift can yield 401s. Ask them to log local time vs NTP.

rivertown_lead: Good call, will check NTP. Quick update: after adding simple lease and 100-500ms jitter to preflights, 200 parallel runs now show <5% 429s and no 401s so far.

sophie_cs: Amazing, thanks team. I'll keep the temporary quota request pending until tomorrow and follow up with a short doc for Rivertown with these mitigations. :thumbsup:

devin_sdk: If they want a long-term fix, we can add an example in the browser SDK to enable ephemeral-lease mode. Filing a small RFC.

alex_eng: Also note for eng: consider a backoff rule in preflight-service to accept small bursts but queue them briefly (200-500ms) to smooth spikes.

rivertown_lead: Will test more and post final results. Thanks everyone!

sophie_cs: Closing loop later today — tag me if anything else shows up. :white_check_mark:
